name: Abihud
overview: Abihud was a male descendant of the tribe of Judah, noted primarily as the son of Zerubbabel in the messianic lineage recorded in Matthew 1:13. His mention in Scripture establishes his place within the genealogical line leading to Christ, emphasizing his role in God's redemptive plan. There are no additional notes or personal details provided about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Abihud means '[my] father has majesty,' reflecting a recognition of God's sovereign authority. This proper name, as recorded in Matthew 1:13, was not given directly by God but carries a meaningful declaration of divine majesty inherent in the name itself.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Abihud as the son of Zerubbabel and the father of Eliakim, as stated in Matthew 1:13. These relationships place him firmly within the genealogical line of Judah leading to the Messiah. Beyond these connections, no further family relationships are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Abihud's significance lies in his position within the genealogy of Jesus Christ, highlighting the fulfillment of God's promise through the tribe of Judah. As a descendant of Zerubbabel, a key figure in Israel's restoration, Abihud represents a link in the chain of God's providential plan culminating in the Messiah. His mention in Matthew underscores the continuity and faithfulness of God's redemptive work through generations.
